body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to Neovim!
  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

## Problem
Continue separators normalization, and try to keep it at the
nvim <-> external boundary, e.g., `fn.xxx`, `api.xxx`, `:xxx`

## Solution
some key changes
- normalize `$HOME-windows`
- entry points of changing directory
  - `nvim_set_current_dir()`, `chdir()`
- normalize the named pipe
  - `--listen` arg, `--server` arg, `:restart`
  - `serverstart()`, `sockconnect()`, `serverstop()`
- make `expand()`, `fnamemodify()` respect 'shellslash' again
- clean up `did_set_shellslash`
- replace `forward_slash` with `TO_SLASH`
- remove obsolete `TMP_PATHSEPSTR`

note
- these funcs still apply `slash_adjust` on return, as before:
  `:pwd`, `chdir()`, `exepath()`, `getcwd()`
- these funcs alwarys return `/`, unlike before the normalization PRs
  `finddir()`, `findfile()`, `getcompletion()`, `glob()`, `globpath()`

close #23639, close #32590

comment_data.body: `expand()` may return backslashes, which can be inconsistent with `/` in buf name (common cases). But if I use `:gs?\\?/?` here, it could also replace backslahes too aggressively, e.g. buf name is `term://xxxC:\cmd.exe`.
not sure whether `tbl_map` is safe here, its docs mention that `is not guaranteed to be stable, even when the data doesn't change`. I use it because I saw similar usage in other cases. :)

comment_data.body:
i would expect lower-level stuff like `changedir_func` to do the `TO_SLASH`. when we do things at higher layers (e.g. in the api, `nvim_set_current_dir`), the fixes are piecemeal and spread around.

is there a reason that `changedir_func` can't enforce slashes ?
similar case: what happens if we enforce slashes in `buflist_add` (the lower layer), instead of `f_bufadd` (the higher layer)? does it break a lot of stuff?

> does it break a lot of stuff?

Probably not, just because the original idea was to move normalization as close to the system boundary as possible. I also considered whether a similar approach like `XFILE` could be applied at the `fn/api` layer (even converting slashes in-place to reduce `TO_SLASH_SAVE`), but I wasn't sure it would be worthwhile, or whether the trade-offs would outweigh the benefits. 🤔
putting it inside is fine. I went back and forth on this a couple of times myself, I'll move it in tomorrow. :D

> because the original idea was to move normalization as close to the system boundary as possible

for *output*, yes, we want to make the decision as "late as possible" (ideally never: leave it up to the user).

for *input*, we achieve a bigger "shield" if the decision is made by core functions, where it makes sense to do so. we don't want to have to patch (and test) every random (new) API function.

but it's also somewhat tricky, because if we do it at a low-level, then we're potentially doing lots of wasteful "conversion", and that also conflicts with the idea that "core should be able to assume `/` slashes".

😩 idk what's best in this case, just thinking out loud.

I  fully agree. Given the current situation, keeping some conversion in the core functions is fine. The separator consistency is already better than before, and it also helps clean up quite a bit of code.

I had a somewhat unrealistic idea that it'd be nice if normalization at the `api/fn` layer were just a matter of declaring a special param type. BTW, I feel the changes around `eval_vars` and `modify_fname` are not ideal. I'll revisit them in the next few days. :)

Regarding the named pipe changes, I haven't moved `TO_SLASH` down yet. I only did a quick experiment today, and it doesn't seem as centralized or simple as the `changedir_func`. However, if we don't want to keep that consistency, we could also just revert those changes.

Not clear what this is testing. If it's just testing pipe slashes, can't it be a 1-line assertion in the existing :connect tests(s)? This is a rather minor detail of :connect.

If it's testing that connecting to a pipe *works* on windows, i'm surprised if we don't already have a test for that, but in that case the test name `'normalizes named pipe #39382'` is misleading.

comment_data.body: This is in intentional, I [previously made](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39155#pullrequestreview-4303356257) `fnamemodify` always return `/`. On the other hand, I wonder if it makes sense to encourage users to use `:S` instead. I recently tested the commands mentioned in #39382, and many of them already have partial support for `/` in paths when they're quoted. Adding the quotes is already one of the things `:S` does. If we want to support backslashes for `cmd.exe`, I feel it would be much simpler to handle the conversion in `:S` than with the current approach. That way, everything else could consistently return `/`. Although that might be pushing `:S` beyond its original purpose?

> On the other hand, I wonder if it makes sense to encourage users to use `:S` instead.

So far, I feel the PR is ready for early review, event though there are still some details that could be improved. I split out 2 separate commits to they can be easily reverted if we decide they aren't needed.
BTW, `fix_slashes` usage has been reduced from 90+  down to 12, and the failing test checks looks unrelated to this PR . :)
I started looking this today. Besides the rebase, I also want to reword some comments and clean up some style inconsistencies (e.g. `(xxx):format(x)`), it'll probably take another day or two. :D

The failing tests pass on my mac. I'm not sure yet why `windows (functional)` timed out. Locally, only `man_spec.lua` hangs for me (I have `msys64/usr/bin/man` in my `PATH`), but the CI env doesn't seem to have a `man.exe`. 🤔

Do you have access to a decent AI? It is useful for spot-checking potential issues. I'm sharing a review from claude below:


<details>
<summary>AI review</summary>

  ## 🔴 Blocking — stack overflow in `f_chdir` (eval/fs.c)
  ```c
  char cwd[MAXPATHL];
  STRCPY(cwd, argvars[0].vval.v_string);  // unbounded copy of user string into fixed buffer
  ```
  `:call chdir(repeat('a', 10000))` overflows the stack. Master passed the pointer directly to `changedir_func` (safe). Fix:
  ```c
  if (xstrlcpy(cwd, argvars[0].vval.v_string, sizeof(cwd)) >= sizeof(cwd)) {
    return;  // too long; mirrors old fail behavior
  }
  ```
  (Added `v_string == NULL` guard is a good touch.)

  ## 🟡 Verify — autocmd full-path branch lost normalization
  The unconditional `forward_slash(fname)` tail block was removed. `sfname` and special-event `fname` now use `TO_SLASH_SAVE`, but `fname = FullName_save(...)` and `fname = xstrdup(buf->b_ffname)` no longer normalize. Safe only if both
  already yield `/` on Windows. `FullName_save` isn't touched in this PR — confirm a Windows test drives a non-special event through it.



</details>
